item.title: Supply Chain Compromise
item.dc:creator: Arctic Wolf
item.description: What Is a Supply Chain Compromise? A supply chain compromise occurs when threat actors infiltrate an organization by targeting and exploiting a trusted third-party vendor, partner, or software provider. Rather than attacking their ultimate target directly, attackers compromise a less secure element in the supply chain and use that foothold to reach multiple downstream organizations simultaneously. These ... Supply Chain Compromise

item.title: Botnet
item.dc:creator: Arctic Wolf
item.description: What Is a Botnet? A botnet is a network of bot‑compromised machines that can be controlled and used to launch massive attacks by a bot‑herder. Formed from the words robot and network, a botnet can be used for mass actions like distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, cryptomining, malware infections, or to crash a network. ... Botnet

item.title: Brute-Force Attack
item.dc:creator: Arctic Wolf
item.description: What Is a Brute-Force Attack? A brute-force attack is a tactic used by threat actors to gain unauthorized access to an account, system, or encrypted data by systematically trying every possible password, encryption key, or credential combination until the correct one is found.
